analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 802-1610). The only change in the file_changes patch is a documentation-only addition at head lines 2492-2512, which describes Flint constrained-decode chaining, mask caching, the automatic paged list entry for RecursiveSI/flint-int4, and fused decode kernels. The patch touches no code, configuration, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior, so there is no security-relevant change to the threat model and no finding. The head text of the changed section was not supplied, so I assessed only the patch excerpt. Points I checked against the threat model: (1) The mask cache is keyed by constraint state and reuses device masks. It holds token-allowed sets only, and the description says it is state-derived, so it is not prompt content. It does not interact with T-041, the prefix-cache scope or the SSD tier. (2) The claim of an identical token stream to unchained decode, with redraw from retained logits, concerns correctness. T-007 and T-056 already say app-reported correctness is not cryptographically proven. (3) Adding flint-int4 to the automatic paged list raises its starting serving width on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra. That affects availability and memory, which relate to T-010 and T-029, but the docs say memory admission and KV budgets are unchanged, and the claim cannot be verified from this evidence. (4) The fused kernels are claimed to give byte-identical outputs. That is unverified and falls outside this documentation-only change. The base-side content (deadlines, MTP, calibration, SSD staging) is unchanged context and I did not treat any of it as new. Remaining question: whether the code behind these doc claims (Flint constraint chaining, fused-kernel numerics, paged-list membership) was changed in other files and needs separate review. None is in this batch.
